subject: Dedicated capacity fit assessment — notes & ask
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@acme.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity fit assessment — notes & ask

Hi Alex / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the candid conversation about performance and isolation needs. Below is a concise recap of the pain points you described, the success criteria you want us to validate for Dedicated capacity, and the immediate asks to get a sizing + commercial proposal over to you.

Key pain points (what you told us)
- Unpredictable tail latency during marketing spikes; current p95 varies and causes a poor UX for customers.
- Cost volatility from multi-tenant burst traffic on shared endpoints.
- Need strong data isolation and controls (audit logs, KMS) for regulated customers; SOC2 is a minimum and a subset of traffic may require HIPAA protections.
- High operational effort to tune autoscaling and manage cold-starts for KV caches.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Model: internally finetuned Llama-2 13B-ish (quantized), served via Triton + FastAPI endpoints today.
- Infra: EC2 GPU-backed fleet for batch + inference; some on-prem model runtime for sensitive workloads.
- Observability: Prometheus + ELK, but traces for per-token latency are limited.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit (what we agreed to validate)
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms for typical prompt distribution (we heard this as your goal; you indicated 200ms acceptable for a small subset).
- Throughput: sustain ~100 TPS baseline with predictable performance; ability to burst to ~400–500 TPS for 5–15 minute windows during campaigns.
- Isolation: VPC-level network separation + dedicated GPU pools; support for SOC2 controls and an option for Private deployment for HIPAA-sensitive traffic.
- Cost predictability: committed monthly capacity with clear billing for burst usage.

Recommended Redwood approach (initial thoughts)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) mapped to an instance/size profile tuned for your model family and token lengths.
- Autoscaling policy: reserved baseline + short-duration burst buffer (configurable minutes) to handle campaigns without immediate scale-out that would violate isolation assumptions.
- KV-cache warmers + prefix caching to reduce cold-start tail latencies for common prompts.

Immediate asks / next steps we discussed
1) Please share an anonymized 7–14 day telemetry extract (CSV) with: per-request timestamp, request token length, average tokens out, p95 latency, and tag indicating whether the request is production-eligible for HIPAA. This will let us run a quick sizing pass.
2) Confirm approximate sustained TPS, observed concurrency, and typical burst duration (ballpark numbers are OK).
3) Schedule a 45–60 minute technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer and our Solutions team (Karthik) — proposed window: Tue 2026-03-10 or Wed 2026-03-11.
4) Procurement: flag any contractual must-haves (data residency clauses, DPA/HIPAA terms) so we can pull the right legal templates.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_capacity_onepager.pdf, estimated_pricing_template.xlsx (attached)

Tentative timeline: if we get telemetry by Wed 2026-03-10, we can return a preliminary sizing and committed-capacity quote within 3 business days.

I’ll loop in Karthik for scheduling and initial sizing once you confirm preferred deep-dive slots and share telemetry.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
https://redwood.com

From: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Mar 2026 09:24:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity fit assessment — notes & ask

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and answers inline:

- p95 target: yes, 120ms is our internal target for the majority of user-facing flows. We can tolerate up to ~200ms for heavy analytic prompts during campaigns.
- Sustained throughput: average ~100 TPS globally for inference. Peak baseline windows can get to 120–150 TPS depending on time of day and region.
- Concurrency: typical request concurrency ~30–50 (we currently cap at ~40 per model endpoint).
- Burst profile: campaign-driven bursts historically have hit ~400–500 TPS for ~5–10 minutes. We need any burst strategy to avoid significant degradation of isolation for enterprise customers.
- Model: we serve a quantized 13B Llama-2 variant; KV-cache sensitivity is high — cold cache adds 2–3x latency on some prompts.
- Compliance/residency: primary region is us-east-1; we have a small set of customers requiring HIPAA controls — if Dedicated is the only way to meet that, we need to understand the Private/VPC options and any on-prem possibilities.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm which AWS regions you currently offer Dedicated in (we prefer us-east-1, us-west-2)?
2) Ballpark committed monthly cost ranges for a profile that would meet the above (we understand a precise quote needs sizing call). Would like a top-line monthly commit vs. pure pay-as-you-go delta.
3) Autoscaling: can the burst buffer be tuned to guarantee reserved pool isolation (i.e., bursts do not pull capacity from other customers)?

I’ll try to get the telemetry extract by Tue; if not, we should still lock the deep-dive so Karthik can see our infra and perf dashboards.

Thanks,
Alex Rutherford
Head of ML, Acme.ai
alex.rutherford@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity fit assessment — notes & ask

Alex — great questions. Quick answers + concrete next steps so we can keep momentum:

Quick answers
- Regions: we currently operate Redwood Dedicated in us-east-1 and us-west-2 for GA customers; we can prioritize proximity to your primary workloads.
- Ballpark pricing: for a committed profile sized to sustain ~100 TPS with burst buffer to 500 TPS (short windows), expect a committed monthly range in the low six-figure USD band. We will provide a detailed quote after the sizing exercise — the attached "estimated_pricing_template.xlsx" shows how burst minutes and reserved vCPU/GPU profiles affect unit cost.
- Autoscaling & isolation: Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools with a configurable burst buffer. Bursts can be satisfied from an allocated burst pool tied to your reservation (no noisy-neighbor spillover) — we can show policy configs in the deep-dive.
- Private/HIPAA: yes — Redwood Private (VPC + optional on-prem agent) is the path for HIPAA-sensitive traffic. That will involve a Private deployment conversation and SOW.

Proposed next steps (actionable)
1) Technical deep-dive (45–60m) — Karthik will lead to review telemetry, perf dashboards, and model runtime details. Proposed slot: Wed 2026-03-11 10:00 AM ET (2026-03-11T10:00:00-04:00). Please confirm or propose an alternate.
2) Pre-call deliverables from Acme: anonymized telemetry CSV (per-request rows), example prompt set (10–20 samples), and a short list of HIPAA-eligible customer IDs (anonymized). Aim to get these by Wed 2026-03-10 EOD.
3) Post-deep-dive: Redwood will return a preliminary sizing doc and a draft committed-capacity quote within 3 business days.

I’ve attached a short agenda for the technical deep-dive (tech-deepdive-agenda.docx) and reattached the pricing template. Karthik / Dev, can you coordinate the meeting invite and bring an outline of kernel/quantization options that reduce p95 tail latency?

Alex — if you can confirm Wed 10am ET and share the telemetry link, I’ll lock the meeting and route a preliminary commercial sketch to procurement.

Best,
Marissa
